category_title: Beginning communicators with complex support needs and complex communication needs who struggle with attention
minimal_context: The teacher and student are participating in a shared reading session using a book and communication devices.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's read 'All You Need for a Snowman'. Look at all this snow! Hit your switch to turn the page.

STUDENT: (Hits the single message voice output device with a fisted hand to respond to the direct request, sitting back in his manual wheelchair.)

TUTOR: Good job. Now look at this big snowman. Is he cold?

STUDENT: (Uses a head nod to answer the yes or no question, but otherwise remains a passive observer.)

TUTOR: Pay attention to the story, Cody. Use your communication board to tell me about the snowman.

STUDENT: (Shows no interest in his personal aided AAC device. He turns his head to the side to refuse, demonstrating disinterest and non-engagement as he struggles with attention.)

options.A: Make expectations clear while respectfully communicating a desire to hear what the student has to say during the shared reading session.
options.B: Simply ask the student if things were tough at home last night before continuing with the shared reading session.
options.C: Attribute meaning to the student's unaided forms of communication and demonstrate symbolic equivalents using his aided AAC device.
options.D: Ask the student how he will respond to the author or what other sources of evidence might contribute to his understanding of the story.
